Priya: quick RFC follow-up — we debated local-vs-central fallback for canary/A-B rollouts. leaning hybrid but want to capture tradeoffs and a minimal interface. local = immediate low-latency failover, central = global budget + de-dupe. thoughts?
Diego: local is great for pod/rack blips. central wins for multi-tenant/global coordination. main worry is state sync + split-brain.
Sam: +1. proposal: local does fast path (3 retries + immediate fallback), central adjudicates longer-lived evictions & budgets. escalate on threshold.
Maya: ops request: need one clear "escalated-fallback" signal in telemetry (trace id + decision reason). also want per-tenant opt-outs for central overrides.
Priya: sketch of arbiter surface:```proto
service FallbackArbiter {
  rpc ReportEvent(ReportRequest) returns (ReportResponse);
  rpc QueryAction(QueryRequest) returns (Action);
}
```and local config example:```yaml
local_fallback:
  max_fast_retries: 3
  escalate_after_ms: 150
  jitter_window_ms: 50
```
infra-bot: deploy-bot: metrics hooks for report_event and query_action endpoints exist on staging. :white_check_mark:
Diego: partition scenario: if control plane unreachable many locals may escalate simultaneously -> can blow downstream capacity. mitigation: jittered escalation + central token-bucket that limits global escalations and returns soft-deny so locals fall back to safe-mode.
Sam: think we should add short-lived "grace leases" central can hand out so clients stay pinned to variant during temporary turbulence (lease TTL ~30s). prevents oscillation during probe windows.
Maya: also add observability contract: 
- metric: fallback.escalated.count (tags: tenant, variant, reason)
- span: fallback.decision (attrs: source=local|central, latency_ms, trace_id)
Priya: next steps: Diego prototype jittered-escalation + token-bucket; Sam draft lease API + client semantics; Maya write telemetry contract and example dashboards; I'll consolidate into a tiny RFC addendum. target: prototype by EOD Fri. @Diego @Sam @Maya add any constraints or blockers. :wave:
